column1: # Names for the 58503A 3704 image, for SmartClockSetup.java, seeded from
# matches tools/firmware/image_diff.py finds between the two images
# (docs/firmware/58503a-3704.md; PLAN.md, "a second image is ported by
# copying the first's work").  Each carried row keeps the Z3805A's name,
# source, note, prototype and convention, its note ending in how it was
# matched.  A note's addresses, and an address its source gives, are the
# Z3805A's unless the note says otherwise.  tools/firmware/seed_names.py
# writes this file and modules.tsv by these rules, make seed-names;
# make check-image-diff fails while they are not what the matches give,
# so a rule or an exception is changed there, not a row here.
# - A function matched identical or relocated (the same bytes, or the
#   same with every outward address masked), or inside one such, is
#   carried; so are the call rows inside one, and its local rows, the
#   Z3805A's stack offsets kept (masking leaves frame offsets as they
#   are).  An installer copy's note gives its primary's 58503A address,
#   where its primary is carried, and its offset from it, "in this
#   image"; a copy said to be byte for byte is checked so.
# - A function matched changed at a similarity (image_diff's difflib
#   ratio of the instructions, numbers masked) of 0.70 or more is
#   carried, noted "changed", for the next wave to review.  From 0.50
#   to 0.70 the Z3805A's name suffixed _58503a marks the pairing as a
#   lead, without its prototype or convention; below 0.50 there is no
#   row, and the pairing is listed under "Leads" at the end.
#   It corrects four more, which the image settles, and carries them
#   under their names: the Oncore decoders oncore_visibility_message,
#   pairs by their shape, are 0x50716, 0x50924 and 0x50968, the message
#   selftest_gps_with_lamp, which image_diff pairs by its bytes with the
#   power test's, 0x18efa, is 0x18ed6, the self-test table's GPS entry
#   (0x18814), which tests a long.  The table also names
#   image_diff pairs the first with the EEPROM's and finds the others
#   missing; supplies_test is 0x186da, which both call.  Routines
#   image_diff pairs at another's last instructions or finds missing
#   are carried where the 58503A's callers name them: selftest_init,
#   0x238b0 and 0x23a3c, one store ahead of the Z3805A's (image_diff
#   takes the stores after it); enter_installer at 0x130da, which
#   deletes fpnl first (image_diff takes its trap #11); return_zero at
#   0x29246, the handlers' (image_diff takes an uncalled tail at
#   0x28d98); scpi_console_port at 0x28db4 and the installer's at
#   installer::0x10739c, the port layer's for port 2 (image_diff takes
#   the tails of the session starts); monitors_reset at 0x23dc2,
#   timecode_schedule at 0x140d0, scpi_task at 0x294cc and the
#   and gps_script_lookup at 0x4c80e, each by its caller or table.
#   sci_echo_none, an rts image_diff finds at qspi_fpga_byte_write's end
#   (0x1f328), has no row: the 58503A has no SCI.
# - A ROM table (a typed label in the image) matched identical or
#   relocated is carried, but not one placed by its bytes alone and
#   under 8 bytes long.  A RAM or I/O label is placed by the matched
#   code's references: an instruction aligned between a Z3805A function
#   and its counterpart (identical, relocated, or changed at 0.70 or
#   more) that names an address in the label, at its start if any does,
#   gives the 58503A's address; it is placed where at least two such
#   references agree, or one in an identical function, and more agree
#   than on any other address.  Labels placed at one address are all
#   dropped, and so is one whose references inside it outvote those at
#   its start, but for nv_settings, which grew, and duartb and
#   installer_duartb, whose fields are rearranged within the same span:
#   they are placed by their start's references, their notes giving
#   installer_duarta_ring is dropped too, though placed by two
#   references, both from one changed piece: at 0x10af1a it would
#   overlap installer_duartb and run past installer_task_spoo.  The
#   58503A's installer keeps no channel A ring (installer::0x103a16).
#   The functions whose few bytes match at more than one address are
#   pinned where the 58503A's callers name them: status_event_hook, a
#   bare rts, at 0x2f1b8, which status_report and status_happening call,
#   where image_diff takes 0x2f1fc; duartb_echo_none at 0x1d3d0, which
#   duart_init and duartb_reconfigure store as duartb.echo, for
#   hook, for 0x45cde; output_state_program and pulse_program at
#   scpi_message_done and scpi_input_closed, which image_diff swaps, at
#   0x290ac and 0x290b0, by scpi_interpret's calls, and the installer's
# - Missing functions, and tables or labels not placed so, have no row;
#   the functions image_diff finds new are listed, unnamed, at the end,
#   with the 8 a bare import's analysis finds called that image_diff
#   neither matches nor finds.  image_diff rejects a start that is text,
#   a table of pointers (the health monitor's channel table, 0x2238a,
#   among them), inside a ROM table it places or inside another
#   function's instructions, so that none of those is listed.
# - A row whose note says "written by hand for the 58503A 3704" is kept
#   as it is, in place of the row the matches give at its address and
#   kind (and name, for a local or call row), or, with none there, after
#   the carried rows; the rest are the seeding's, which make
#   check-image-diff checks.  A hand row may take a name the matches give
#   another place only where a hand row takes that place too.  The types
#   wave's hand rows place the RAM
#   labels the rules leave unplaced where the 58503A's code shows them,
#   type tables the 58503A sizes otherwise, and give changed functions
#   the locals whose frames the 58503A's code bears out, each note
# Tab-separated: address, function or label, name, the source that gives
# it, and optionally a note saying what it is or does, a C prototype or
# a label's type, and a function's calling convention.  A "local" row
# instead gives the function at its address a stack variable: its name,
# and "TYPE @ OFFSET", Ghidra's offset from the stack pointer at entry,
# in the prototype field.  A "call" row gives the call through a
# pointer, or a variadic call, at its address its callee's prototype.
# The convention is key=value pairs separated by "; ":
#   convention  c, register, exception, pforth, psos-service, other or
#               undetermined; a function without one is unknown
#   confidence  run, read, documented, derived or assumed; KEY.confidence
#   in, out     items separated by ", ": a register, high first for a
#               pair (D0:D1), then optionally a type and a name; an item
#               without a register is a stack argument
#   copies      registers the result is also left in, high first
#               (A0:A1); SmartClockExportC.java gives a caller's C them
#   returns     ccr, for the condition codes
#   results     registers it also leaves results in, past out;
#               SmartClockExportC.java gives a caller's C them
#   error       items: a register, a value, what it means
#   family      the routines it belongs with
# A register prototype is built from in and out, and only at run, read
# or documented; the prototype field takes no "@".
